text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some basic rules. First, use clear and simple endpoints, such as /users or /orders/123, so developers can easily understand them. Second, always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also important because it helps other people use your API without confusion. Finally, remember to use versioning, for example /api/v1/, so you can improve your API in the future without breaking existing applications. These practices make your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
